newsitem.title: POLAND: Popularity of Poland's PM falls after floods - poll.
newsitem.headline: Popularity of Poland's PM falls after floods - poll.

text.p: The popularity of Polish Prime Minister Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz has declined, just a month before general elections, as voters give the thumbs down to his government's handling of last month's floods, opinion pollsters said on Tuesday.

The prime minister's approval rating sank four points to 36 percent in August, with 48 percent dissatisfied with his performance, according to a survey commissioned by the Rzeczpospolita newspaper from the private PBS institute.

Dissatisfaction increased six points from the previous poll in July, when critics of Cimoszewicz outnumbered those who approved of his performance for the first time since he took office in February 1996, PBS said.
PBS said the prime minister's popularity had been harmed by the government's handling of July's flooding, which killed 54 people in Poland and caused billions of dollars of damage.

"Without doubt it was the flood that made the prime minister's popularity fall, as well as a public debate over the government operations and the prime minister's own comments in the media," PBS deputy head Ryszard Pienkowski told Reuters.

Cimoszewicz declared, before the full extent of the flooding became clear, that ruined farmers should have been insured and could expect no help from state reserves. He later apologized for his comments.

A PBS poll released on Monday showed support for Cimoszewicz's party, the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), down one point to 25 percent as it fell behind the opposition Solidarity Election Action alliance, which gained three points to 28 percent.
But Pienkowski said growing criticism of the performance of Cimoszewicz would have a limited impact on the SLD's chances in the September 21 elections.
"The popularity of Cimoszewicz among SLD voters has not changed radically and 70 percent of its supporters expressed their approval in August," he said.
